text:
nora.kim: quick notes from today's design sync on dedicated-pool autoscale + policy compiler. capturing decisions and owners.

diego.santos: high level: compile tenant policy -> small set of numeric goals + ranked actions. keep DSL orthogonal to scheduling logic.

priya: add a burst_budget primitive so tenants can burst without exceeding monthly caps. e.g. burst_budget_seconds: 3600.

ollie: watch for double-accounting with warmup credits. compiler should emit separate fields for burst_budget vs warmup_credit usage.

nora.kim: operator compatibility: compiled intent includes version and short hash. operator treats unknown versions as best-effort when feature-flagged.

priya: observability requirement: every enforcement decision must include policy_id, compile_version, and decision_code in the span.

ollie: conflict resolution: deterministic ordering by sla_tier then weighted tenant score. soft vs hard constraints; compiler marks them explicitly.

diego.santos: special case: hardware limits (MIG/thermal) can make goals infeasible. compiler should emit feasibility_estimate based on recent pool telemetry.

nora.kim: rollout plan: (1) schema behind flag, store policies for 10d; (2) compiler in staging pools 1w; (3) operator logs + provenance integrated with alerts 2w; (4) expand and flip after 3w with no regressions.

priya: dashboards before enforcement: false-positive evictions, unexpected throttles, burst burn-rate, compile mismatch errors.

ollie: simulator tasks: simulate mixed-tenant policies, compute fairness and cost distribution. reuse cluster-sim harness with policy resolver.

diego.santos: owners: diego -> compiler spike (4d), ollie -> sim scenarios, nora -> schema+storage, priya -> observability.

runtime-bot: lint-check: schema draft validated locally; feature-flag disabled.

nora.kim: i'll post RFC addendum with sample proto, rollout timeline, and monitoring checklist. reconvene after spikes. :thumbsup:
